title: Iman Gadzhi on the cost of building big: chaos, seasons of life, and stacking agency, education and software
summary: Long personal interview covering Iman's childhood, mental health and relationships. The business-relevant parts: top-level performance carries a permanent stress tax, test a new path part-time before going all in, and how he stacked an agency, an e-learning company and software.

principles.text: Operating at the top level means a permanently stressed mind; there is no escaping that trade-off.
principles.quote: if you're trying to perform at the top top top top level your mind is going to be a Minefield and there's no getting past that

principles.text: Define success by your current season of life, and accept what you neglect while you focus.
principles.quote: success means living in accordance to the season of your life so this season of my life is about taking on this burden and taking on the stress

principles.text: Prove a new path with a couple of hours a day before quitting everything; go all in only when you have little to lose.
principles.quote: I don't see why you can't start a business or start your next career step with two hours a day and prove to yourself first that you want it

principles.text: Passive income is borrowed time: front-loaded work decays as markets change, so keep options to pivot.
principles.quote: what you're doing is you're buying yourself time I might put in a lot of work now for six months and that front loads two years of success but eventually that's going to start to Decay and crumble

principles.text: Stack businesses along the customer journey: an education front end feeds the software those customers need next.
principles.quote: I had my e-learning business and you get paid on the run in because agency is the model that worked for me and on the back end what solution are they going to use it was agency flow

principles.text: Raising prices without adding value, because someone else (like the government) funds the buyer, erodes the industry.
principles.quote: it's any business in general that increases prices without trying to add extra value
